cultural_entities.gloss: Traditional Indian bangles, typically made of glass, metal, or lacquer, worn by women on the wrists. They hold deep cultural, social, and symbolic significance in South Asia, often associated with femininity, marriage, and festive celebration, and are celebrated for the distinct chiming sound (khanak) they make when they clink together.
negative_confusions: Thick, heavy modern Western-style single bracelets or cuffs
visual_features: Typically thin and worn in multiples or sets on each wrist
Vibrant colors (often red, green, gold, or multi-colored)
Made of glass or polished metal reflecting light

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The specific onomatopoeic quality of 'chanakti' (clinking/tinkling of bangles) and 'khanak' (metallic/glass ring) is flattened into the more generic English 'chime' and 'sound'.

The translation shifts 'sapna neendon mein utarta hai' (a dream descends into sleeps/slumber) to 'a vision descends in quiet streams' to force an English rhyme, losing the pluralized intimacy of 'neendon' (sleeps) and replacing 'dream' with 'vision' and 'quiet streams'.

The translation alters 'bahakta hai' (wanders, goes astray, becomes intoxicated/wild) to 'sways... in time', which reverses the original sense of uninhibited, drifting movement to one of structured rhythm.

stanzas.loss_note: The translation of 'kasak' as 'yearning that lingers after' captures the emotional essence but loses the specific, sharp physical-emotional ache implied by the Hindi word.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation adds 'that lingers after' to 'yearning' (kasak) to complete a rhyme scheme, which is not present in the original Hindi text.
The translation of 'kasak' as 'yearning' partially misses the physical/emotional nuance of a dull, lingering ache or sudden twinge of pain/longing.
The repetition of the opening couplet in L7-L8 carries the same loss of 'chanakti' and 'bahakta' (altered to 'chime' and 'sways... in time') as seen in Stanza 1.

annotation.theme: The sensory memory of a beloved's bangles evoking deep emotional resonance and longing.

original_poem:
तुम्हारे हाथ की चूड़ियाँ जब छनकती हैं,  
जैसे कोई गीत हवा में बहकता है।  
उनकी खनक में जैसे कोई रंग बिखरता है,  
जैसे कोई सपना नींदों में उतरता है।  

उनके हर रंग में तुम्हारी हँसी की झलक है,  
हर छनक में जैसे दिल की कोई कसक है।  
तुम्हारे हाथ की चूड़ियाँ जब छनकती हैं,  
जैसे कोई गीत हवा में बहकता है।
translated_poem:
When the bangles on your hands chime,  
It's as if a song sways in the air, in time.  
In their sound, colors scatter like dreams,  
As if a vision descends in quiet streams.  

Each hue reflects a glimpse of your laughter,  
Each chime holds a yearning that lingers after.  
When the bangles on your hands chime,  
It's as if a song sways in the air, in time.
